clusters.reason: Around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991 and the months before and after: your grandfather Clifford coming back into the family in early 1989, your move to Quarry Lane and then to the rebuilt Hollin Road house, your late nights and drop in functioning through secondary school, your mother filling in your college forms, your close friendship with Rafe tightening and then breaking apart after your wrist injury stopped your playing, your anxiety rising and functioning falling as you moved into first term, and a welling up of low mood with no footing by early 1992 alongside your sister Tara's birth. clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer diagnosis, 2001–2003
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer found in 2001 or 2002 and the months after: your running out of steam for performing, your disastrous audition for the national orchestra in early 2002, your distance from your parents and friends, your move to Gull Harbour, your meeting Marisol at a winter party and moving to Fenwick to live with her, the split within the year, and your sinking into a deep depression once back in Thornbury. clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death, 2008
clusters.reason: Around your grandmother Lorna's death in early January 2008 and the months after: the building work at Alder Creek with Silas in the summer, your distance from your mother when you could barely manage a phone call, her pressing to visit you there and the conflict when she arrived at your door, your cutoff from her when you moved to Marlow Sound for nursing school in September, and your aunt Imogen's stroke in early 2009. The silence with your mother held for roughly a year before settling.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: Around your marriage to Wren in March 2017 and the months after: your contact with your mother easing off slightly once Wren came along, your cousin Alice's diagnosis of multiple sclerosis in October 2017, and in October 2019 a burst of events around Wren's mother's retirement party at the lake: Wren swamped by one thing after another, your overfunctioning to settle her, her tight fusion with her father and brother, your sleep collapsing at the lake weekend with no sleep from the small hours and only pulling back as others rose, and her anxiety rising as you both drove home in a long quiet afterward. These shifts sit close together in the same weeks and months; the cluster settles once the weekend passed and plans were made.
